articles.title: Pretraining Transformers with Quantized Softmax in Attention
Why Your AI Agents Burn Billions of Tokens (with Tyler Cox and Ish Shah)
articles.description:
#agenticai  #AItokenomics #localai 

In Episode #1031, Ish Shah and Tyler Cox (Distinguished Engineers in the Office of the CTO for Dell Technologies' client group) join @JonKrohnLearns to work out why agentic AI bills are exploding and what can be done about it. Over one weekend Ish burned roughly two billion tokens on a side project, and that is the ordinary shape of agentic work now: agents spawn sub-agents, the pie of work grows, and cheaper tokens only invite more ambitious projects. Tyler runs a small Dell lab that pushes hundreds of millions of tokens a day through local hardware instead. In this episode, they define what makes a system agentic, explain how to read a Pareto curve when choosing models, work through the jagged frontier and why most tasks do not need a frontier model, and lay out what moving agentic workloads onto your own hardware does to the economics.

This episode is brought to you by: 
• ODSC, the Open Data Science Conference: https://odsc.ai/west/
• Anthropic: https://claude.ai/superdata

In this episode you will learn:

• (00:00:00) Introduction
• (00:03:42) What makes a system agentic
• (00:12:45) Picking the right model for the task
• (00:17:58) How to read a Pareto curve
• (00:28:00) Why agents burn so many more tokens

304: How to Build a Manufacturing Company from First Principles with Supersede CEO Sean Petterson
articles.description:
RVs are homes that go 60 miles an hour. That changes everything about what goes inside them.

Chris sits down with Sean Petterson, CEO of Supersede, a company combining recycling and manufacturing in an unexpected way - turning recycled plastic into structural building materials. Supersede started with boats, where wood has an obvious problem - boats get wet!

From there, the company moved into RVs, where the materials face constant movement and thermal cycling, on a production line that can build an entire RV in a couple of hours.

Sean also explains the thinking behind Supersede's manufacturing model, including why he'd rather build 10 smaller plants than one big one.

In this episode, find out:

  • How running production lines in mirrored pairs cuts the distance operators walk across the floor
  • Why an RV, built to go 60 miles an hour, is a harder test for a material than a house that never moves
  • How Supersede built its own ERP with zero software developers, piecing it together through Slack, Jira, and GitHub instead
  • How a pre-sold capacity threshold - already dropping fast - decides when Supersede builds its next plant
  • How embedding machine vision and LiDAR on the line replaces a QA machine that would otherwise cost far more
  • Why Sean thinks manufacturers who didn't start using AI a year ago are already a decade behind

Enjoying the show? Please leave us a review here. Even one sentence helps. It’s feedback from Manufacturing All-Stars like you that keeps us going!

Tweetable Quotes:

  • "If you hadn't gotten on the AI bus 12 months ago, you're a decade behind." - Sean Petterson, CEO of Supersede
  • “A big contributor to those inefficiencies is, frankly, just legacy that gets embedded.” - Sean Petterson, CEO of Supersede
  • “In manufacturing, things can move slow, and we just have the unique benefit of making sure that we're investing effectively, but very efficiently.” - Sean Petterson, CEO of Supersede

Links & mentions:

  • Supersede is a manufacturing company turning recycled plastic into structural building materials, starting with its Marine Board product for the marine and RV industries.
  • Harmoni is a factory orchestration platform that connects what's happening on your shop floor with the systems you already use, from your machines and operators to your ERP, giving your team one real-time view of production.
  • PTC's Industrial Newsletter - a quick hit of clarity on how design, manufacturing, and service data can work together for manufacturing leaders looking to modernize.

Make sure to visit http://manufacturinghappyhour.com for detailed show notes and a full list of resources mentioned in this episode. Stay Innovative, Stay Thirsty.
